_note: Chapters 1-5 = 30 concepts. SVG vocabulary: viewBox 0 0 160 160, stroke=currentColor, width 2.6, round caps. Accent fills use var(--acc). No text elements below 11px.

entries.title: API Request Structure
entries.picture: One envelope with the entire correspondence stuffed inside.
entries.analogy: You never post just the reply. You post the whole conversation again — every letter either of you has ever sent, re-copied, with the new one on top. The postal service has the memory of a goldfish and charges you by weight.
entries.snapback: Every request carries model, max_tokens and messages[] — and messages[] is the full history, not the latest turn.

entries.title: Message Roles
entries.picture: Letters alternating down one table, each signed by one of two hands.
entries.analogy: Two correspondents, strictly taking turns. Slip a letter into the pile signed with the other hand and the model will read it back as something it said itself — and carry on from there quite happily.
entries.snapback: user and assistant alternate inside messages[]. The system prompt is not a role in that array.

entries.title: The stop_reason Field
entries.picture: A postmark franked on the returned envelope, telling you what happens next.
entries.analogy: The postman does not write 'I think that's everything' in cursive at the bottom of page four. He stamps the outside: DELIVERED, or NEEDS A SIGNATURE. You read the stamp. You do not read the handwriting and form an impression.
entries.snapback: Branch on stop_reason: tool_use → run the tool and loop; end_turn → stop. Never parse the reply text for a sign-off.
entries.svg: <path d='M14 46h132v70H14z'/><path d='M14 46l66 40 66-40'/><circle cx='118' cy='42' r='26' fill='var(--acc)' opacity='.18'/><circle cx='118' cy='42' r='26' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><path d='M108 42l7 8 14-16'/><path d='M28 130h40M84 130h48' opacity='.5'/>

entries.title: System Prompt
entries.picture: A notice screwed above the sorting desk that every item passes under.
entries.analogy: It is not in the post. It is bolted to the wall above the bench, and every single item travels beneath it on the way through — including the one you send in an hour, and the one after that.
entries.snapback: The system prompt is a top-level parameter sent with every request. Persona, tone and standing behavioural rules belong there.
entries.svg: <rect x='26' y='14' width='108' height='44' rx='4' fill='var(--acc)' opacity='.16'/><path d='M26 14h108v44H26z'/><path d='M40 28h80M40 38h80M40 48h48'/><path d='M56 58v10M104 58v10' opacity='.5'/><path d='M14 92h132' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M30 78h30v14H30zM68 78h30v14H68zM106 78h30v14h-30z'/><path d='M45 100v14M83 100v14M121 100v14' opacity='.4' stroke-dasharray='3 5'/>

entries.title: Context Window
entries.picture: A mail sack with a hard brim you cannot pack past.
entries.analogy: One sack, one size. A longer conversation does not earn you a bigger sack — it earns you a fuller one, and everything already in there gets carried again on every future trip.
entries.snapback: The window bounds the entire request: system prompt + full history + tool definitions + the reply. Growth costs latency and money on every turn.

entries.title: What is tool_use
entries.picture: A numbered docket that has to come back pinned to the plate.
entries.analogy: Claude does not cook. It writes a docket — table four, one lasagne — and pushes it through the hatch. Nothing happens until the kitchen actually cooks, and the plate comes back with that same number still pinned to it.
entries.snapback: The model emits a tool_use block; your code runs it and returns a tool_result carrying the same id.

entries.title: Tool Definition
entries.picture: Two dishes on a menu — one described properly, one merely named.
entries.analogy: 'Soup' next to 'Soup' tells a diner nothing at all. 'Chilled cucumber, no dairy, starter' next to 'slow beef broth, main' tells them everything. Nobody is guessing from the name — they are reading the description underneath it.
entries.snapback: Tool descriptions are the model's primary basis for selection. State what it does, what input it takes, when to use it, and when not to.

entries.title: The tool_choice Parameter
entries.picture: Three doors out of the same restaurant.
entries.analogy: auto lets you sit down, chat, and leave having eaten nothing. any runs a door policy — you are not getting out without ordering something, though the dish is entirely your call. Naming a tool is the tasting menu: the first course was settled before you walked in.
entries.snapback: If the question says guarantee, auto is out. If it also wants the model to pick which schema fits, it is any.

entries.title: JSON Schemas for Structured Output
entries.picture: A plating diagram taped inside the pass.
entries.analogy: Protein here. Sauce there. Three spears, not four. Anything leaving the kitchen has to match the diagram, and there is no negotiating about it at the hatch.
entries.snapback: Make the tool's input_schema the shape you want back. Required versus nullable decides whether the model may return nothing instead of inventing something.
entries.svg: <circle cx='80' cy='84' r='58' stroke-dasharray='6 5' opacity='.5'/><circle cx='80' cy='84' r='46'/><circle cx='66' cy='72' r='16' fill='var(--acc)' opacity='.2'/><circle cx='66' cy='72' r='16' stroke-dasharray='4 4'/><rect x='88' y='62' width='26' height='20' rx='3' stroke-dasharray='4 4'/><path d='M62 104h36' stroke-dasharray='4 4'/><path d='M70 100v8M80 100v8M90 100v8'/><path d='M16 22h30M16 22v10M144 22h-30M144 22v10' opacity='.55'/><path d='M50 16h60v14H50z' fill='var(--acc)' opacity='.16'/><path d='M50 16h60v14H50z'/>

entries.title: Syntax vs Semantic Errors
entries.picture: Two plates: one obviously wrong, one plated perfectly with the wrong fish.
entries.analogy: The pass catches the first before it leaves the kitchen. The second walks straight out to the table, because it matches the diagram in every measurable way. Only the person who ordered cod finds out.
entries.snapback: Schemas eliminate the syntax class outright and do nothing for the semantic class. Valid JSON still holds a wrong number.

entries.title: What is an Agentic Loop
entries.picture: A clapperboard with a loop arrow: shoot, watch it back, decide, go again.
entries.analogy: The director is not working through a fixed list of takes. They shoot one, watch it on the monitor, and that is what tells them whether there is a next one.
entries.snapback: Send → inspect stop_reason → execute any tools → append the results → send again, until end_turn.

entries.title: AgentDefinition Configuration
entries.picture: A crew lanyard: name, job, and exactly which kit you may sign out.
entries.analogy: The badge says who you are, what you are here to do, and which three items from the equipment cage you are allowed to take. The cage does not care what your job description aspires to.
entries.snapback: name/description, system_prompt, allowed_tools. The tool list is a whitelist, and least privilege per subagent type is the whole point.

entries.title: Hub-and-Spoke: Coordinator and Subagents
entries.picture: Every line runs through the chair in the middle. The crew-to-crew line is crossed out.
entries.analogy: Camera does not brief sound. Sound does not brief wardrobe. It all goes through the person in the chair — which is precisely how that person knows what happened when something goes wrong at 2am.
entries.snapback: Subagents never communicate directly. The coordinator sees every exchange, handles errors uniformly, and controls what each subagent receives.
entries.svg: <circle cx='80' cy='80' r='22' fill='var(--acc)' opacity='.18'/><circle cx='80' cy='80' r='22'/><path d='M72 74h16M72 82h16M72 90h10' opacity='.7'/><circle cx='80' cy='20' r='13'/><circle cx='140' cy='80' r='13'/><circle cx='80' cy='140' r='13'/><circle cx='20' cy='80' r='13'/><path d='M80 33v25M127 80h-25M80 127v-25M33 80h25'/><path d='M32 32l36 36' opacity='.35' stroke-dasharray='4 5'/><path d='M40 30l-14 14M26 30l14 14' stroke-width='2.2'/>

entries.title: The Task Tool for Spawning Subagents
entries.picture: Two directors — one issued a radio, one not.
entries.analogy: You can write 'delegates freely to the crew' into somebody's job description all day long. If nobody handed them a radio, they will quietly do the entire job themselves and you will never hear a word about it.
entries.snapback: A coordinator's allowedTools must include Task. No prompt can grant a tool that the configuration withholds.

entries.title: Hooks in the Agent SDK
entries.picture: A safety officer who physically stops the take before it rolls.
entries.analogy: They do not advise. They do not hope. They stand in front of the camera when the shot breaks the rules, and they do it whether or not the director agrees, on every single take.
entries.snapback: PreToolUse runs before and can block or modify. PostToolUse runs after and reshapes the output. Deterministic code — not an instruction.

entries.title: What is MCP
entries.picture: One socket shape, three very different appliances.
entries.analogy: Before the standard, every appliance shipped with its own strange prongs and its own adapter you inevitably lost. The standard does not make the kettle boil faster. It means the kettle plugs into anything without a bespoke lead.
entries.snapback: MCP is the open protocol connecting Claude to external tools, readable data and prompt templates through one interface.
entries.svg: <rect x='54' y='96' width='52' height='48' rx='6' fill='var(--acc)' opacity='.16'/><rect x='54' y='96' width='52' height='48' rx='6'/><circle cx='70' cy='116' r='5'/><circle cx='90' cy='116' r='5'/><path d='M70 128h20'/><path d='M80 96V76'/><path d='M40 40h80v22H40z'/><path d='M56 62v14M80 62v14M104 62v14'/><rect x='30' y='16' width='24' height='24' rx='4'/><rect x='68' y='12' width='24' height='28' rx='4'/><circle cx='118' cy='28' r='13'/><path d='M56 28h12M106 28h-14' opacity='.5' stroke-dasharray='3 4'/>

entries.title: MCP Servers
entries.picture: An appliance with buttons on the front and a booklet in the side pocket.
entries.analogy: The server is the machine. Its buttons are the things you can make it do. It came with a booklet you can read without pressing anything, and a card of pre-written settings for common jobs.
entries.snapback: One server exposes three primitives: tools (actions you call), resources (data you read), prompts (reusable templates).
entries.svg: <rect x='22' y='34' width='92' height='96' rx='7'/><rect x='36' y='50' width='64' height='24' rx='4' fill='var(--acc)' opacity='.2'/><circle cx='48' cy='96' r='9'/><circle cx='68' cy='96' r='9'/><circle cx='88' cy='96' r='9'/><path d='M44 116h48' opacity='.5'/><path d='M120 56h26v54h-26z' fill='var(--acc)' opacity='.12'/><path d='M120 56h26v54h-26z'/><path d='M126 68h14M126 78h14M126 88h9'/><path d='M114 82h6' opacity='.6'/>

entries.title: Configuring MCP Servers
entries.picture: The building's wiring versus the extension lead you brought from home.
entries.analogy: The wiring is in the walls — everyone who moves in inherits it. The lead in your bag is yours alone, which is fine right up until you assume your teammate has one too.
entries.snapback: .mcp.json at project root is version-controlled and shared. ~/.claude.json is yours only. ${VAR} keeps credentials out of the repo.

entries.title: The isError Flag in MCP
entries.picture: A lit fault light beside an appliance that simply produced nothing.
entries.analogy: 'It broke' and 'it worked, and there was genuinely nothing in there' look identical from across the room, and they lead you to do opposite things. One deserves another go. The other is your answer.
entries.snapback: isError: true when the query could not run. Zero matches is a success with an empty result — never an error.
entries.svg: <rect x='14' y='40' width='58' height='84' rx='6'/><circle cx='43' cy='60' r='9' fill='var(--acc)' opacity='.5'/><circle cx='43' cy='60' r='9'/><path d='M43 55v6' stroke-width='2.4'/><circle cx='43' cy='66' r='1.3' fill='currentColor'/><path d='M28 86h30M28 98h30M28 110h18' opacity='.55'/><path d='M34 34l4-10M52 34l-4-10' opacity='.7'/><rect x='88' y='40' width='58' height='84' rx='6'/><circle cx='117' cy='60' r='9'/><path d='M100 90h34v26h-34z' stroke-dasharray='5 5'/><path d='M108 103h18' opacity='.5'/>

entries.title: MCP Resources
entries.picture: Reading the contents page, versus pressing every button to find out what the machine does.
entries.analogy: You can discover the menu by pressing all fourteen buttons and watching what happens. Or you can read the two-page contents list that came in the box, and then press exactly the one you needed.
entries.snapback: Resources hand the model a readable map of what data exists, without spending tool calls on exploratory guessing.

entries.title: The CLAUDE.md Hierarchy
entries.picture: Three notes from three floors, all ending up in the same hand.
entries.analogy: Building rules, flat rules, room rules. You do not reach the room and discover the building rules have evaporated — you are holding all three at once. If two of them disagree, that is now a piece of paper you have to go and fix.
entries.snapback: The levels concatenate from root down to the working directory. There is no override precedence between them.

entries.title: @path Syntax (File Imports)
entries.picture: A note that says 'see the green folder', and the green folder.
entries.analogy: Instead of one enormous laminated sheet nobody reads, the fridge note points at the folder that actually holds the detail. Chains work — up to a point, and that point is five.
entries.snapback: @./path/file.md inlines another file. Relative paths resolve from the file doing the importing. Maximum nesting depth is 5.
entries.svg: <rect x='14' y='34' width='48' height='60' rx='4' fill='var(--acc)' opacity='.14'/><path d='M14 34h48v60H14z'/><path d='M24 50h28M24 62h28M24 74h16'/><path d='M62 64h26' stroke-dasharray='0'/><path d='M80 56l10 8-10 8'/><rect x='94' y='34' width='48' height='60' rx='4'/><path d='M104 50h28M104 62h28M104 74h16' opacity='.7'/><path d='M30 106v10h100v-10' opacity='.5'/><path d='M40 122h16M64 122h16M88 122h16M112 122h16' opacity='.5'/><text x='80' y='142' font-size='13' fill='currentColor' stroke='none' text-anchor='middle' font-family='monospace'>max 5</text>

entries.title: The .claude/rules/ Directory
entries.picture: Notes taped to individual doors. Only the one you walk through lights up.
entries.analogy: The bathroom note is invisible until you are actually in the bathroom. Brilliant when a rule genuinely only concerns bathrooms. Useless for 'shoes off at the front door', which has to live on the fridge where everyone passes it.
entries.snapback: Rules load on file-path glob match. If the question is not about which files, it is not rules.

entries.title: Custom Slash Commands and Skills
entries.picture: A labelled box you take down from the cupboard when you actually need it.
entries.analogy: It does not run your household. It sits on the shelf with its name printed on the front until somebody asks for it by name.
entries.snapback: Project commands in .claude/commands/ ship with the clone. Personal ones in ~/.claude/commands/ do not. $ARGUMENTS carries whatever was typed after the name.

entries.title: Skills — .claude/skills/
entries.picture: The spec printed on the inside of the box lid.
entries.analogy: Inside the lid: what this thing is, what to type after its name, which tools it is allowed to touch, and whether it makes its mess in a separate room.
entries.snapback: SKILL.md frontmatter: description, argument-hint, allowed-tools, context: fork. Tool scoping lives here — not in .mcp.json.

entries.title: Planning Mode vs Direct Execution
entries.picture: Surveying the wall versus hammering one nail.
entries.analogy: You measure before knocking through a supporting wall. You do not commission a structural survey to hang a picture. And you do not start swinging, then call the surveyor once it gets frightening.
entries.snapback: Plan mode for large or multi-approach work; direct execution when the scope is clear. Switching reactively mid-job is the documented trap.

entries.title: The /compact Command
entries.picture: A thick diary squeezed thin, with the dates falling out of the side.
entries.analogy: You keep the plot. You lose 'three hundred and ten pounds, due on the twelfth'. Which is entirely fine, right up until the next thing you do turns on it being three hundred and ten pounds due on the twelfth.
entries.snapback: /compact compresses context and can drop exact values, dates and specifics. Do not run it immediately before work that needs the precision.

entries.title: The /memory Command
entries.picture: Fanning out the rulebooks you are actually holding, and spotting the gap.
entries.analogy: Before arguing about why the rule is not being followed, check whether the page carrying the rule is in your hand at all. Very often it turns out to be on somebody else's fridge.
entries.snapback: /memory lists the memory files actually loaded. First diagnostic step whenever behaviour differs between machines or between sessions.

entries.title: Claude Code CLI for CI/CD
entries.picture: One terminal prints and exits. The other sits there blinking forever.
entries.analogy: A pipeline has nobody at the keyboard. Without the flag that means 'answer and go', it waits politely for a human who is never coming, and the build times out at 3am.
entries.snapback: -p/--print runs non-interactive. --output-format json with --json-schema makes the output parseable. --batch and CLAUDE_HEADLESS do not exist.

entries.title: fork_session and Session Management
entries.picture: One save point, two branches that never touch again.
entries.analogy: You spent two hours mapping the dungeon. You are not doing that again to try the other door — you save, and you branch.
entries.snapback: fork_session gives divergent branches from one shared baseline. --resume continues a named session; tell it which files changed if the code moved underneath it.
